intent: Revert sensor y to 0.04 (the iteration 2 row) and keep the 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.05 m, since the y = 0.06 test brought back line loss. Change one thing relative to the best design: wheel_track 0.12 to 0.15 m, to test whether more turning authority reduces the steady 0.061 m excursion. I expect line loss to stay at zero and max_error to fall below about 0.058 m, with a score at or above 26.99. I am considering, without committing, a lighter mass (about 0.6 kg) to reduce yaw inertia if max_error does not move with wheel track. I am not changing body width, because the off-track floor stays at 0.06 m.
learning: Iteration 3 showed that look-ahead y = 0.06 does not reduce max_error (still 0.061 m) and brings back line loss on the s-bend and slalom, so y = 0.04 stays. Still open: whether turning authority (wheel_track) or mass sets the steady excursion. The Integrator should report the signal range and whether the excursion appears at the start of the run or at a specific bend, since that separates a transient from a steady-state offset.
rationale: Iteration 3 moved sensor y from 0.04 to 0.06 and scored 26.62, below iteration 2's 26.99. Line loss returned on the s-bend and slalom (1 event each), and max_error stayed at about 0.061 m on every track. The longer look-ahead therefore did not reduce the excursion and reintroduced line loss. Iteration 1 showed that span removes line loss, and iteration 2 showed that footprint does not move max_error. Following the Integrator's contingency, I revert y to 0.04 and keep the 16 mm footprint at x = ±0.05 m, which is the best-scoring geometry so far. I also add one change to test the Integrator's remaining lever: wheel_track from 0.12 to 0.15 m, for more turning authority. The off-track floor is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), and body_width cannot lift it above 0.06 m, so the body stays at 0.12 m. Mass and body are unchanged. This is a deliberate deviation from the Integrator's plain revert, which I can take because it still starts from the best-known row. Expected result: max_error falls below about 0.058 m with line loss at zero. If max_error stays at about 0.061 m, the wheel track is not the lever either, and the next test should be mass or the start-up transient.
